summary.en: Israeli artillery and airstrikes continue hitting southern Lebanese towns such as Wadi Zibqin while Hezbollah persists in firing and is expanding its arsenal, including reported shipments to Yemen. Israel has reallocated $90 million from border-community recovery budgets to defense and is delaying completion of the Lebanon border wall. US sanctions on Hezbollah affiliates are viewed as having limited impact, and Iran is reported to be developing chemical weapons. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israelsk artilleri og luftangrep fortsetter å treffe sørlige libanesiske byer som Wadi Zibqin mens Hizbollah fortsetter å skyte og utvider sitt arsenal, inkludert rapporterte forsendelser til Jemen. Israel har omfordelt 90 millioner dollar fra budsjetter for gjenoppbygging av grenseområder til forsvar og forsinker ferdigstillelsen av grenseveggen mot Libanon. Amerikanske sanksjoner mot Hizbollah-tilknyttede anses å ha begrenset effekt, og Iran skal utvikle kjemiske våpen. Konflikten har forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
